react_result.final_narrative_text: The metabolomics differential set of ten compounds was interrogated across three complementary enrichment paradigms: RaMP multi-database ORA (Reactome + SMPDB + KEGG + WikiPathways), mummichog m/z-direct network activity against the human metabolic function network (MFN), and MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific pathway-set enrichment. All five steroid hormones in the input (dihydrotestosterone, testosterone, androstenedione, dehydroepiandrosterone, and estradiol) produced a powerfully convergent signal across paradigms. RaMP ORA identified 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' (KEGG:map00150 / SMPDB:SMP00068) as the top pathway with FDR = 2.16 × 10⁻¹⁴ and fold-enrichment = 1250.9 — a signal driven by all five steroids hitting a 27-member pathway roster. The same pathway appeared as rank-1 'Androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism' in mummichog (p = 0.00294) with 9/9 input steroid metabolites mapping to a 9-member MFN module, and as the top KEGG hit hsa00140 in MetaboAnalystR with the identical five steroid hits. Mummichog additionally resolved a secondary signal around thromboxane A2 (KEGG:C02198) embedded in the prostaglandin formation and arachidonic acid metabolism modules (rank 2, p = 0.020). InChIKey reconciliation confirmed zero structural conflicts across all eight resolved compounds, validating that the cross-tool agreement reflects genuine biological overlap rather than namespace artefacts. The biological story is one of broad disruption of C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism — a pathway that interlinks adrenal androgen precursors (DHEA, androstenedione) through to active androgens (dihydrotestosterone, testosterone) and the aromatase-derived estrogen (estradiol) — alongside secondary eicosanoid-axis perturbations.

{
  "narrative_text": "The metabolomics differential set of ten compounds was interrogated across three complementary enrichment paradigms: RaMP multi-database ORA (Reactome + SMPDB + KEGG + WikiPathways), mummichog m/z-direct network activity against the human metabolic function network (MFN), and MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific pathway-set enrichment. All five steroid hormones in the input (dihydrotestosterone, testosterone, androstenedione, dehydroepiandrosterone, and estradiol) produced a powerfully convergent signal across paradigms. RaMP ORA identified 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' (KEGG:map00150 / SMPDB:SMP00068) as the top pathway with FDR = 2.16 × 10⁻¹⁴ and fold-enrichment = 1250.9 — a signal driven by all five steroids hitting a 27-member pathway roster. The same pathway appeared as rank-1 'Androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism' in mummichog (p = 0.00294) with 9/9 input steroid metabolites mapping to a 9-member MFN module, and as the top KEGG hit hsa00140 in MetaboAnalystR with the identical five steroid hits. Mummichog additionally resolved a secondary signal around thromboxane A2 (KEGG:C02198) embedded in the prostaglandin formation and arachidonic acid metabolism modules (rank 2, p = 0.020). InChIKey reconciliation confirmed zero structural conflicts across all eight resolved compounds, validating that the cross-tool agreement reflects genuine biological overlap rather than namespace artefacts. The biological story is one of broad disruption of C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism — a pathway that interlinks adrenal androgen precursors (DHEA, androstenedione) through to active androgens (dihydrotestosterone, testosterone) and the aromatase-derived estrogen (estradiol) — alongside secondary eicosanoid-axis perturbations.",
